A possession cannot be the owner's partner or claim the owner's due.","anchor":"خلقا وملكا وتصرفا ليس لأحد سواه عزوجل إستقلالا ولا شركة","mentions":[]},{"verses":["31:26"],"words":["إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلْغَنِىُّ"],"type":"meaning","speaker":"author","stance":"holds","claim":"Al-Ghani means independent of everything.","anchor":"إن الله هو الغني ( عن كل شيء","mentions":[]},{"verses":["31:26"],"words":["ٱلْحَمِيدُ"],"type":"meaning","speaker":"author","stance":"reports","claim":"Al-Hamid means deserving praise even if no one praises Him, or praised in actuality by every creature through its state.","anchor":"المستحق للحمد وإن لم يحمده جل وعلا أحد أو المحمود بالفعل","mentions":[]},{"verses":["31:26"],"words":["إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلْغَنِىُّ ٱلْحَمِيدُ"],"type":"rhetoric","speaker":"author","stance":"holds","claim":"The emphatic clause answers a suspicion that God owns creation because He needs it: He is fully independent; al-Hamid signals His beneficence and perfections.","anchor":"وكأن الجملة جواب عما يوشك أن يخطر ببعض الأذهان السقيمة","mentions":[]},{"verses":["31:26"],"words":["لِلَّهِ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ"],"type":"interpretation","speaker":"الطيبي","stance":"reports","claim":"Al-Tibi says the ownership statement belittles idolaters and shows God needs neither them nor their praise and worship; al-Ghani is independent of worshippers' praise, while al-Hamid means worthy of praise whether praised or not.","anchor":"إن قوله تعالى ( لله ما في السموات والأرض ) تهاون بهم","mentions":[]}]}
